goal: Implement the Canvas2D renderer core: layered draw queue, sprite + sprite-sheet + animation player, and a camera. Pixel-perfect at 480x270 logical resolution. Documented in docs/03-TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 (engine/render/).
constraints: Renderer exposes: `clear()`, `drawSprite(sprite, x, y, layer)`, `flush()`. Draw calls are queued by layer and emitted in layer order during `flush()`.
Layers (ordered): bg, world, entities, fx, ui, debug.
Atlas loader parses the project's JSON atlas format: `{ image: string, frames: { [name]: {x,y,w,h,duration?} } }`.
AnimationPlayer advances frames based on a tick in seconds; supports loop, once, ping-pong; emits a `complete` callback for non-loop.
Camera follows a world-space target with optional dead-zone; supports shake (frequency + decay).
All draw positions snapped to integer pixels.
Test environment: jsdom + a stubbed CanvasRenderingContext2D that records calls.
acceptance: Renderer `flush()` produces draw calls in correct layer order in a stubbed-canvas test.
Animation `ping-pong` test verifies frame sequence over 1.5 cycles.
Camera shake test verifies decay reaches < 0.1 within the configured duration.
verification: bash -c 'npm run lint --silent && npm run typecheck --silent && npm run test --silent -- src/engine/render'
